newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bourse to extend margin rules until end-Dec.
newsitem.headline: Thai bourse to extend margin rules until end-Dec.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) on Thursday agreed to extend its 25 percent call margin and 15 percent forced sale rules until December 31, a SET spokesman said.
SET spokesman Suvicha Mingkwan told a news conference that the SET board had agreed to the rules because of the prevailing sluggish stock market.
The SET board last December agreed that the 25 percent call margin and 15 percent forced sale rules would expire at the end of June this year.

The spokesman said the extension of the forced sale rule, under which brokers are permitted to force indebted clients to sell off shares in order to raise funds to repay debts to brokerages, was made due to the sluggish bourse.
The SET index, which dropped to a new eight-year low last week, has plunged 15 percent this month and lost 32.5 percent since January.
The SET board also decided to lend 2.5 billion baht ($96 million) to Thai Securities Finance Corp (TSFC), which will use funds to buy equity margin loan accounts from brokerage firms.
TSFC's purchase of margin accounts will help inject liquidity into the securities companies, which are short of cash due to the battered stock market, the spokesman said.
"The SET board will consider lending additonal money, if TSFC wants more funds," he said.
